Card AI vs CollX: what does the price represent?

A scan can identify the right card and still leave a pricing question. Compare how each app records the copy you own and explains the value you see.

Variant, condition and price are separate decisions

QuestionCard AICollX
Which printing?Suggests catalog candidates for you to confirmIts FAQ says it shows multiple variants for selection and offers manual search
What condition?You choose a raw condition or enter the grade on an existing slabIts FAQ says users manually enter condition or grade; it does not assess condition from a scan
What does the value use?Published market price for the confirmed record and available history; sports cards may link to eBay searchIts FAQ describes marketplace transactions, a median from recent sales, fallback last sale, and an estimate when direct sales are absent
What happens next?Keep distinct holdings in a portfolioAdd to collection; CollX also documents its marketplace

A useful test with two copies of one card

Take one raw copy and one PSA slab of the same printing. In each app, confirm the exact variant, enter the raw condition or slab grade, and note whether the displayed figure is a current estimate, a last sale or a historical trend. This makes an appraisal question concrete. Neither a scanner result nor a marketplace estimate authenticates the card.

CollX is a fit if its built-in buy, sell and trade workflow matters to you. Card AI focuses on reviewed catalog records, condition-specific holdings and collection value. Both products support sports cards; neither should be described as uniquely supporting them.

Read the source of the number

CollX explains its median, fallback and estimate rules in its pricing FAQ. Card AI shows its published market price and available history; an eBay link for sports cards opens a separate search and is not a synced feed of sold transactions. Comparing those figures as if they are the same metric can mislead a seller.

Sources were reviewed October 19, 2026. We have not measured recognition or valuation accuracy on matched physical cards.

Card AI vs CollX questions.

Does CollX identify raw card condition automatically?

CollX says in its FAQ that users enter condition or grade manually. Card AI also asks you to select raw condition or an existing slab grade.

Can I use both apps for sports cards?

Yes. CollX documents sports-card scanning, and Card AI supports basketball, football and soccer card workflows.

Are Card AI and CollX prices calculated the same way?

Do not assume so. CollX publishes a median and fallback methodology in its FAQ. Card AI shows a published market price and available history for the selected record; its eBay search link is separate.

Try the collection tracker in Card AI.

Check a raw card and an existing slab separately before adding either to your collection.
